heading: Bill Emerson National Hunger Fellows and Mickey Leland International Hunger Fellows

tree.heading: Short title
tree.text: This section may be cited as the “Bill Emerson National Hunger Fellows and Mickey Leland International Hunger Fellows Program Act of 2008”.

children.heading: Director
children.text: The term “Director” means the head of the Congressional Hunger Center.

children.heading: Fellow
children.text: The term “fellow” means—
a Bill Emerson Hunger Fellow; or
Mickey Leland Hunger Fellow.

children.heading: Fellowship Programs
children.text: The term “Fellowship Programs” means the Bill Emerson National Hunger Fellowship Program and the Mickey Leland International Hunger Fellowship Program established under subsection (c)(1).

children.heading: In general
children.text: There is established the Bill Emerson National Hunger Fellowship Program and the Mickey Leland International Hunger Fellowship Program.

children.heading: In general
children.text: The purposes of the Fellowship Programs are—
to encourage future leaders of the United States—
to pursue careers in humanitarian and public service;
to recognize the needs of low-income people and hungry people;
to provide assistance to people in need; and
to seek public policy solutions to the challenges of hunger and poverty;
to provide training and development opportunities for such leaders through placement in programs operated by appropriate organizations or entities; and
to increase awareness of the importance of public service.

children.heading: Bill Emerson Hunger Fellowship Program
children.text: The purpose of the Bill Emerson Hunger Fellowship Program is to address hunger and poverty in the United States.

children.heading: Mickey Leland Hunger Fellowship Program
children.text: The purpose of the Mickey Leland Hunger Fellowship Program is to address international hunger and other humanitarian needs.

children.heading: In general
children.text: Subject to subparagraph (B), the Secretary shall offer to provide a grant to the Congressional Hunger Center to administer the Fellowship Programs.

children.heading: Terms of grant
children.text: The terms of the grant provided under subparagraph (A), including the length of the grant and provisions for the alteration or termination of the grant, shall be determined by the Secretary in accordance with this section.

children.heading: In general
children.text: The Director shall make available Bill Emerson Hunger Fellowships and Mickey Leland Hunger Fellowships in accordance with this subsection.

children.heading: In general
children.text: The Fellowship Programs shall provide experience and training to develop the skills necessary to train fellows to carry out the purposes described in subsection (c)(2), including—
training in direct service programs for the hungry and other anti-hunger programs in conjunction with community-based organizations through a program of field placement; and
providing experience in policy development through placement in a governmental entity or nongovernmental, nonprofit, or private sector organization.

children.heading: Work plan
children.text: To carry out subparagraph (A) and assist in the evaluation of the fellowships under paragraph (6), the Director shall, for each fellow, approve a work plan that identifies the target objectives for the fellow in the fellowship, including specific duties and responsibilities relating to those objectives.

children.heading: Bill Emerson Hunger Fellow
children.text: A Bill Emerson Hunger Fellowship awarded under this section shall be for not more than 15 months.

children.heading: Mickey Leland Hunger Fellow
children.text: A Mickey Leland Hunger Fellowship awarded under this section shall be for not more than 2 years.

children.heading: In general
children.text: Fellowships shall be awarded pursuant to a nationwide competition established by the Director.

children.heading: Qualifications
children.text: A successful program applicant shall be an individual who has demonstrated—
an intent to pursue a career in humanitarian services and outstanding potential for such a career;
leadership potential or actual leadership experience;
diverse life experience;
proficient writing and speaking skills;
an ability to live in poor or diverse communities; and
such other attributes as are considered to be appropriate by the Director.

children.heading: In general
children.text: A fellow shall receive—
a living allowance during the term of the Fellowship; and
subject to subparagraph (B), an end-of-service award.

children.heading: Requirement for successful completion of fellowship
children.text: Each fellow shall be entitled to receive an end-of-service award at an appropriate rate for each month of satisfactory service completed, as determined by the Director.

children.heading: Terms of fellowship
children.text: A fellow shall not be considered an employee of—
the Department of Agriculture;
the Congressional Hunger Center; or
a host agency in the field or policy placement of the fellow.

children.heading: Emerson Fellow
children.text: An individual awarded a fellowship from the Bill Emerson Hunger Fellowship shall be known as an “Emerson Fellow”.

children.heading: Leland Fellow
children.text: An individual awarded a fellowship from the Mickey Leland Hunger Fellowship shall be known as a “Leland Fellow”.

children.heading: Evaluations and audits
children.text: Under terms stipulated in the contract entered into under subsection (c)(3), the Director shall—
conduct periodic evaluations of the Fellowship Programs; and
arrange for annual independent financial audits of expenditures under the Fellowship Programs.

children.heading: In general
children.text: Subject to paragraph (2), in carrying out this section, the Director may solicit, accept, use, and dispose of gifts, bequests, or devises of services or property, both real and personal, for the purpose of facilitating the work of the Fellowship Programs.

children.heading: Limitation
children.text: Gifts, bequests, or devises of money and proceeds from sales of other property received as gifts, bequests, or devises shall be used exclusively for the purposes of the Fellowship Programs.

tree.heading: Report
tree.text: The Director shall annually submit to the Secretary of Agriculture, the Committee on Agriculture of the House of Representatives, and the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry of the Senate a report that—

children.text: describes the activities and expenditures of the Fellowship Programs during the preceding fiscal year, including expenditures made from funds made available under subsection (g); and
includes the results of evaluations and audits required by subsection (d).

tree.heading: Authorization of appropriations
tree.text: There are authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary such sums as are necessary to carry out this section, to remain available until expended.

notes.heading: Codification
notes.text: Pub. L. 110–234 and Pub. L. 110–246 made identical amendments to this section. The amendments by Pub. L. 110–234 were repealed by section 4(a) of Pub. L. 110–246.

notes.heading: Amendments
notes.text: 2008—Pub. L. 110–246, § 4401, amended section generally, substituting subsecs. (a) to (g) establishing the Bill Emerson National Hunger Fellowship Program and the Mickey Leland International Hunger Fellowship Program for former subsecs. (a) to (j) which established the Congressional Hunger Fellows Program. 2007—Subsec. (f)(4)(A). Pub. L. 110–161, which directed that subpar. (A) be amended by substituting “may” for “shall” and striking out “annual.”, was executed by making the substitution and striking out “annual” before “audit”, to reflect the probable intent of Congress.

notes.heading: Effective Date of 2008 Amendment
notes.text: Amendment of this section and repeal of Pub. L. 110–234 by Pub. L. 110–246 effective May 22, 2008, the date of enactment of Pub. L. 110–234, except as otherwise provided, see section 4 of Pub. L. 110–246, set out as an Effective Date note under section 8701 of Title 7, Agriculture. Pub. L. 110–234, title IV, § 4407, May 22, 2008, 122 Stat. 1142, and Pub. L. 110–246, § 4(a), title IV, § 4407, June 18, 2008, 122 Stat. 1664, 1903, provided that: “Except as otherwise provided in this title [see Tables for classification], this title and the amendments made by this title take effect on October 1, 2008.” [Pub. L. 110–234 and Pub. L. 110–246 enacted identical provisions. Pub. L. 110–234 was repealed by section 4(a) of Pub. L. 110–246, set out as a note under section 8701 of Title 7, Agriculture.]

notes.heading: Effective Date
notes.text: Pub. L. 107–171, title IV, § 4405, May 13, 2002, 116 Stat. 341, provided that: “Except as otherwise provided in this title [see Short Title of 2002 Amendment note set out under section 2011 of Title 7, Agriculture], the amendments made by this title take effect on October 1, 2002.”
